chunks: As they will noisily argue in the Fire, the weaker ones will say to the arrogant: 'We were your followers, so will you take over some of our share of the fire?'
ai.seo_question: What do the weak followers say to their arrogant leaders in Hellfire?
ai.summary: In the Shia exegetical tradition, this verse from Surah Ghafir illustrates the ultimate futility of political and spiritual allegiance when the 'tabi'' (followers) confront their 'a'immah' (leaders) in the Hereafter. It underscores that while leaders may have guided the masses, they cannot transfer the burden of individual accountability, emphasizing the personal nature of divine justice. This scene serves as a critical reminder for the community to distinguish between blind following and conscious adherence to truth.
